about: The review's questions for Alessandro, one issue at a time, in rounds. Built into a page by tools/review_issues.py; his decisions land in the page's `issues` collection, one document per key, and are copied here under each issue's `decided`.

rounds.name: Round 1
rounds.title: Eight issues, one at a time
rounds.intro: Each screen is one issue the review found: the page beside our render, what the checks say, what Claude says, and what Claude proposes. The first four are faults no check raises; the last four are false alarms the checks still raise today. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: The review's disagreements with the checks, as eight issues ranked by consequence: four faults no check raises (counted from Claude's review of dev's 83 opened pages and the 31 known), then four false alarms the checks still raise today (each rejected call re-checked on today's code, 2026-11-07, and counted where it is still major). Built into a page by tools/review_issues.py; Alessandro's decisions land in the page's `issues` collection, one document per key.

issues.title: Words drawn in the same colour as their band
issues.what: The page prints “Estimated patient responsibility $2,965.78” in white on a black bar. Our render draws the bar black and the words black, so the patient's total cannot be read.
issues.checks: Nothing. Every word is in the HTML, so no check sees a problem.
issues.claude: A major fault: the reader loses the line.
issues.often: 11 pages: dark bars, header rows and buttons whose words vanish.
issues.proposes: A new check: every line the page prints readable must be drawn with enough contrast against what lies behind it. If not, major.

issues.title: Labels and their amounts pulled apart
issues.what: The page prints each label with its amount on one line. Our render draws the three labels, then the three amounts under them.
issues.checks: Nothing. Every word is there, in an order the checks accept.
issues.claude: A major fault: you cannot tell which amount belongs to which label.
issues.often: 8 pages: totals, price lists, rows joined by leaders.
issues.proposes: A new check: a label and its value printed on one line must be drawn on one line. If not, major.

issues.title: Text drawn on top of other text
issues.what: The receipt prints “Date: 01/10/2021”. Our render draws each label over its value, so the line reads “Dat01/10/2021”.
issues.checks: Nothing. The words are all there, in order.
issues.claude: A major fault: the lines cannot be read.
issues.often: 8 pages: labels over values, signature blocks, chips over chips.
issues.proposes: A new check: two words apart on the page must not overlap in the render. If they do, major.

issues.title: Two boxes side by side, drawn one under the other
issues.what: The page prints “Year to date” and “Time off” side by side. Our render stacks them, and draws Time off as loose lines.
issues.checks: Only the line it lost (“Vacation used 40 h”). No check sees side by side become stacked.
issues.claude: A major fault: the page's layout is lost.
issues.often: 14 pages: cards, header boxes, a list beside its picture.
issues.proposes: A new check: blocks printed side by side must be drawn side by side. If stacked, major.

issues.title: Alignment flagged where nothing moved
issues.what: “Compass Outfitters” is printed at the left, after its logo. Our render draws it at the left too. It wraps on two lines and loses the logo, but those are other faults.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”. The check measured the name against its whole box, and the logo before it made it look pushed to the right.
issues.claude: Not an alignment fault: the name sits where the page puts it.
issues.often: 22 majors still raised on 18 pages: a name after a logo, a clause beside its hanging number, a size inside a chip.
issues.proposes: Raise an alignment fault only when the line itself moves on the page, its left, centre and right edges all more than a few pixels from where it is printed.

issues.title: A size change nobody can see, called major
issues.what: “OFFICE USE” is 11 px on the page and 10.8 px in our render.
issues.checks: Major: “printed at the body's size, drawn smaller than the body”. The page's labels are 11 px and the render's 11.5 px, so 10.8 px falls just under them.
issues.claude: Not a fault: the difference cannot be seen.
issues.often: 12 type majors still raised on 11 pages, most of this kind.
issues.proposes: Raise a size fault only when the line's own size, printed against drawn, differs by more than 10%.

issues.title: A name printed twice, compared with the wrong copy
issues.what: “Camila Park” is printed twice: a script signature (1) and a bold printed name (2). Our render draws both the same way.
issues.checks: Two majors: “script printed, sans drawn” and “sans printed, script drawn”. It compared copy 1 on the page with copy 2 in the render.
issues.claude: Not a fault: each copy is drawn as printed.
issues.often: 36 majors still raised on 4 pages (c0008, c0424, c0345, the payslip).
issues.proposes: Where the same words are printed more than once, pair each copy with the nearest copy in the render, not the first one found.

issues.title: Three columns: the check counts a mix-up 15 times
issues.what: Sections 2, 3 and 4 are printed as three columns, and our render keeps three columns. But it draws item (a) of section 2 in section 3's column, and 4.4 at the bottom under section 2.
issues.checks: 15 majors, one for every pair of sections: “their words alternate in the reading order”.
issues.claude: The 15 are one fault counted 15 times. The real faults are the two items drawn in the wrong column. Claude's first call named only 4.4; on a second look, (a) is out of place too.
issues.often: 20 majors still raised on 4 pages (c0221, c0374, c0384, c0464).
issues.proposes: Where the page sets columns, read the order column by column, and report only the items drawn in another column: here 2 faults, “under another heading”.

rounds.name: Round 2
rounds.title: Round 2: eight more, one at a time
rounds.intro: Your round 1 decisions are recorded: seven agreed, and one disagreed, the alignment issue. Issues 1 to 3 ask about alignment, so Claude learns where your line is; 3 is a fault Claude confirmed. Issues 4 to 6 are severities the criteria leave open. Issues 7 and 8 are spot checks of faults Claude confirmed, to test Claude's own judgement. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 2: issue 1 asks again about round 1's alignment issue, which Alessandro disagreed with; 2-3 are alignment examples (one false alarm, one Claude confirmed); 4-6 are severity questions review-criteria.md does not settle; 7-8 are spot checks of Claude's confirmed majors, drawn at random (seed 0) from the confirmed majors still raised today. Every example re-checked on today's code, 2026-11-07.

issues.title: The name after the logo: what is wrong here?
issues.what: You disagreed with Claude on this one in round 1. The page prints a logo, then “Compass Outfitters” on one line. Our render drops the logo, wraps the name onto two lines, and so starts it about 30 px further left.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”.
issues.claude: The name is still set left. What is wrong is the lost logo and the wrap, and each should be its own fault: a figure lost, a line broken differently.
issues.often: The alignment check raises this kind on 18 pages.
issues.proposes: Report this as the lost logo and the wrap, not as alignment. Disagree if, to your eye, the name's alignment is wrong too, and say so in the note.

issues.title: A menu drawn where the page prints it, called moved
issues.what: The menu “Produit · Tarifs · Clients · Aide” sits at the top right, on the page and in our render. Only the dots between the words are lost.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”.
issues.claude: Not an alignment fault: the menu is where the page puts it. The lost dots are a minor.
issues.often: One of the 22 alignment majors still raised on 18 pages.
issues.proposes: No alignment fault here; one minor for the dots. Raise alignment only when the line itself moves.

issues.title: Values pushed away from their labels
issues.what: The page prints “Jobs: 214    Retries: 19”, each value right after its label. Our render pushes “214” to the right, against “Retries:”, and “£212.40” away from “Cost:”.
issues.checks: Major: alignment, “printed left, drawn right”.
issues.claude: Agrees: a real major fault. The values no longer read with their labels.
issues.often: One of 36 alignment majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it as a major fault.

decided.note: Problem seems more a spacing issue - in this specific case not major since all text is there and right aligned values however have inconsistent distance wrt their same line label which i think is more a minor

issues.title: Justified text drawn ragged: major or minor?
issues.what: The page sets each clause justified, both edges straight, beside a hanging number (1.1, 1.2). Our render sets it ragged on the right, puts the number inline, and adds bullets before 1.2 and 1.3.
issues.checks: Major: “printed justified, drawn left”.
issues.claude: A real fault: Claude's first call rejected it, and on today's check that call was wrong. But a ragged right edge is hard to see. The lost hanging numbers and the added bullets are the bigger change.
issues.often: Justified text is on many pages: letters, contracts, reports.
issues.proposes: Justified drawn ragged: minor. A lost hanging number or added bullets: a structure fault, major.

issues.title: A pill drawn as a full-width band: major or minor?
issues.what: The page prints “Free entry · Family friendly” in a small orange pill. Our render draws an orange band across the whole page.
issues.checks: Nothing: the words are all there.
issues.claude: Major: the band changes how the page looks at a glance. The criteria call a missing fill major, but say nothing of a fill drawn the wrong shape.
issues.often: 6 pages: a band split into boxes, a pill stretched to a band, a card drawn as stripes.
issues.proposes: A fill drawn the wrong shape or size is major, like a missing fill, and a new check catches it.

issues.title: Buttons drawn as plain lines: major or minor?
issues.what: The page prints three buttons, outlined or filled. Our render draws two of them as plain lines between rules, and loses the third.
issues.checks: Only the lost one, “Commencer maintenant”.
issues.claude: Claude was not consistent: major on this page, minor on others. The criteria call “chips drawn as plain text” minor and “a frame missing” major, and a button is both.
issues.often: 7 pages.
issues.proposes: Minor, like chips: the words are there and read the same. A frame missing stays major for boxes that hold content: cards, panels, fields. The lost button is its own major.

issues.title: Values under the wrong header
issues.what: The page's header “Value” spans Min, Typ and Max. Our render shifts the headers, so “Unit” stands over the typical values and the units have no header.
issues.checks: Major: “48” is “drawn under Unit, printed under Typ”.
issues.claude: Agrees: a real major fault. The table reads wrong.
issues.often: One of 6 cell majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it as a major fault.

issues.title: Numbered steps drawn as bullets
issues.what: The page numbers four steps, 1 to 4. Our render draws bullets: steps 1 and 2 lose their numbers, and 3 and 4 keep them after a bullet.
issues.checks: Major: “numbers as bullets”, 4 items.
issues.claude: Agrees: a real major fault. The steps' order is no longer printed.
issues.often: One of 10 structure majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it as a major fault.

rounds.name: Round 3
rounds.title: Round 3: fifteen, one at a time
rounds.intro: Round 2 is recorded: seven agreed, and one disagreed, the values pushed from their labels, which you called spacing and minor. Claude takes that as your line for alignment: a line drawn in another place on the page is major; a shift inside its own column, different spacing or a lost indent is minor. Issues 1 to 5 test that line. Issues 6 to 15 are spot checks of Claude's confirmed majors in the other classes (type, words, lines, rules, order, page height), drawn at random; on two of them Claude now proposes minor. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 3: issues 1-5 test the alignment line Alessandro drew in round 2 (spacing is minor), four from Claude's confirmed alignment majors and one Claude added; 6-15 are spot checks of Claude's confirmed majors, drawn at random (seed 1; the lost lines seed 2) among those still major on today's code, one or two per class.

issues.title: Right-aligned answers drawn beside their questions
issues.what: The page prints each answer at the right edge, joined to its question by a dotted leader. Our render puts the answers in a column right beside the questions, and drops the leaders.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”, 16 lines.
issues.claude: Claude first confirmed it major. By your round 2 line it is minor: every answer is there and reads with its question; what changed is spacing. The lost leaders are a separate minor.
issues.often: One of 36 alignment majors Claude confirmed; many are of this kind.
issues.proposes: Minor: answers drawn beside their questions instead of at the right edge.

issues.title: Times drawn at the left of their column
issues.what: The page sets the times flush right in their column. Our render sets them flush left in the same column.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”, 8 lines.
issues.claude: The criteria's own example of a major alignment fault is exactly this: right-aligned numbers drawn left. By your round 2 note it would be minor: same column, same rows. Your call decides which wins.
issues.often: Numbers in table columns, on many pages.
issues.proposes: Minor, and the criteria's example changes: right-aligned numbers drawn left in their own column is minor.

issues.title: A flag drawn at the column's edge, not its centre
issues.what: The page centres the “H” (high) flag in its Flag column. Our render draws it at the table's right edge, and the column's header shrinks to a speck.
issues.checks: Major: “printed centre, drawn left”, the header and 5 flags.
issues.claude: Minor by your line: same row, same column. The header drawn tiny is a size fault of its own.
issues.often: One of 36 alignment majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Minor.

issues.title: A note moved off the title's line
issues.what: The page prints “Fill in and hand to a Kestrel Makers volunteer” at the right, on the same line as the title “Booking slip”. Our render draws it on its own line under the title, at the left.
issues.checks: Major: “printed right, drawn left”.
issues.claude: Major by your line: the line has moved to another place, not just shifted in its own spot.
issues.often: One of 36 alignment majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Major: a line drawn in another place on the page.

issues.title: A paragraph's first-line indent lost
issues.what: The page indents the first line of every paragraph. Our render sets this one flush; the next paragraph keeps its indent.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Claude added it as a major. By your line it is spacing: minor.
issues.often: Claude added 6 majors of this kind: indents lost, justified text drawn ragged.
issues.proposes: Minor.

issues.title: A small date line drawn at body size, in bold
issues.what: The page prints “Aggiornato il 19 aprile 2023” small and regular under the title. Our render draws it at the body's size, in bold.
issues.checks: Major: “printed smaller than the body, drawn at the body's size”.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The line gains size and weight and competes with the title.
issues.often: One of 87 type majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A small address line drawn twice as large
issues.what: The page prints the clinic's address small, under its name. Our render draws it about twice the size, wrapping onto two lines.
issues.checks: Major: “printed smaller than the body, drawn larger than the body”.
issues.claude: Agrees: major.
issues.often: One of 87 type majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: Tick and cross marks drawn as bullets
issues.what: The page marks three medicines ✓ and one ✗: “Sospesa: ibuprofene” (stopped). Our render keeps the first ✓ and draws the rest as bullets, so the ✗ is lost.
issues.checks: Major: “✓, 2 printed and not drawn”.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The cross carries meaning: this drug is stopped.
issues.often: One of 102 word majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: Subscripts drawn as underscores
issues.what: The page prints the formula with subscripts: H₂₀₁₅, Vₜ. Our render writes them as code: “H_2015”, “V_t”.
issues.checks: Major: the word “h2015” lost.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The formula no longer reads as printed.
issues.often: One of 102 word majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

decided.note: formula is overall correct but misrepresented i guess can just use some reformat to show it as suffix so not major

issues.title: Two checklist lines lost
issues.what: Section 3 prints three ticked statements. Our render draws only the first; the other two are gone.
issues.checks: Major: their words lost.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The two lines fall between two Zones, and no Zone covers them.
issues.often: One of 102 word majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: Lines run together into one paragraph
issues.what: The page prints Forma, Posologia and Quantità each on its own line under the drug. Our render runs them into one paragraph, and breaks “Diagnosi:” away from its text.
issues.checks: Major: line breaks differ in 7 blocks.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The lines no longer read as a list of fields.
issues.often: One of 44 line majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A paragraph wrapped at different words
issues.what: Our render's text column is wider than the page's, so the same paragraph wraps at different words: three lines on both, broken in other places.
issues.checks: Major: “3 breaks added and 3 lost”.
issues.claude: Major by the criteria (“any line breaking at a different word”). But nothing is lost and only the column's width differs; by your round 2 note this could be minor.
issues.often: One of 44 line majors Claude confirmed; many are of this kind.
issues.proposes: Minor where a whole paragraph re-wraps because its column is wider or narrower. Major where lines are joined or split inside a block, as in the previous issue.

issues.title: One empty cell merged with its neighbour
issues.what: In the exams table, “Rx torace di controllo” has an empty Ingresso cell beside it. Our render draws no rule between them, so the label runs into that cell and wraps.
issues.checks: Major: “2 of the 27 rules not drawn”.
issues.claude: Claude confirmed it major. Looking again: the table reads the same, and one missing rule is minor.
issues.often: One of 16 rule majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Minor when a few rules go missing and the table reads the same; major when the table's grid is lost.

decided.note: major - table layout not respected risks data misinterpretation in this case creates confusion

issues.title: A line drawn under the wrong heading
issues.what: The page prints “Christmas week, 24/12/2026 to 01/01/2027” under NO SERVICE. Our render draws it under BEFORE YOU TRAVEL, as if it were a travel tip.
issues.checks: Major: “interleaved”, the two lists' words alternate.
issues.claude: Agrees: major. The meaning flips: there are no buses that week.
issues.often: One of 8 order majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: The page drawn 24% taller
issues.what: Our render is 1,343 px tall against the page's 1,081: about a quarter taller, from larger type and lines that wrap.
issues.checks: Major: “1.24 of the picture's height”.
issues.claude: Agrees: major by the criteria (more than 10% off).
issues.often: One of 31 height majors Claude confirmed.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

rounds.name: Round 4
rounds.title: Round 4: thirteen faults Claude added
rounds.intro: Round 3 is recorded: thirteen agreed. Your alignment line holds on all five cases, and a re-wrapped paragraph is minor. Two disagreed: subscripts drawn as “H_2015” are minor (the formula is right, only shown differently), and one missing table rule is major, because it risks misreading the table. Claude's confirmed majors held on 8 of 10. This round checks the other side: faults no check raised that Claude added on its own, one of each kind you have not seen, drawn at random. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 4: one fault of each kind Claude's review added and Alessandro had not seen, nine major and four minor (letterspacing and small capitals on one page, as one issue), to check Claude's additions. Issue 11 is Claude's minor re-proposed as major, by the criteria's colour rule.

issues.title: A total's label at the top, its amount at the bottom
issues.what: The receipt prints “TOTALE COMPLESSIVO € 44,05” together under the items. Our render draws the label above the item list and the amount at the very bottom, under a column of prices torn from their items.
issues.checks: Nothing for the label's place. The prices torn from their items are round 1's “labels pulled apart”.
issues.claude: Added as major: the total no longer reads as one line.
issues.often: Claude added 7 majors of this kind: a line drawn under another heading or apart from its group.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A summary box drawn without its frame
issues.what: The page frames the three totals in a box and shades Net pay. Our render draws them with dividers only: no frame, no shading.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Added as major: the criteria call a missing frame major, and this box holds content.
issues.often: Claude added 5 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major, and a check for frames the page draws.

issues.title: A serif page drawn in a sans
issues.what: The page sets its title, headings and body in a serif. Our render sets everything in a sans.
issues.checks: Nothing: the type check reads faces from the CSS and misses this one.
issues.claude: Added as major: the criteria call the wrong font class major.
issues.often: Claude added 5 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major, and fix the type check so it sees it.

issues.title: A chart's title drawn twice
issues.what: The page prints “VISITORS LAST ACTIVE WEEK” once, above its chart. Our render draws it as text, and again inside the chart's picture.
issues.checks: Nothing: the picture's words are not read.
issues.claude: Added as major: an invented line.
issues.often: Claude added 4 majors of this kind: a title or headline drawn twice.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: Signing lines not drawn
issues.what: The page draws a line to sign on above “Signature”, “Name and title” and “Date”, for both parties. Our render draws none, and the second party's labels pile onto the first's.
issues.checks: Only the labels drawn over each other.
issues.claude: Added as major: the lines are what the block is for.
issues.often: Claude added 4 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A four-column grid drawn as two columns in tiny type
issues.what: The page sets the project's eight fields in a four-column grid. Our render draws two columns, in type about 7 px high.
issues.checks: Nothing: sizes are checked line by line, and a grid's width not at all.
issues.claude: Added as major: the box's shape and its type both change.
issues.often: Claude added 3 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A headline drawn white on dark boxes
issues.what: The page prints the headline dark on white. Our render draws it white on a dark box behind each line, and misspells “MOUSSES”.
issues.checks: Only the misspelling.
issues.claude: Added as major: a fill the page does not have changes the headline's look.
issues.often: Claude added 3 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A bold red order number drawn black
issues.what: The letter prints “encomenda n.º 2103-118” in bold red. Our render draws it in bold black.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Added as major: the red marks what matters, and the criteria call a colour that carries meaning major.
issues.often: Claude added 3 majors of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: A table's last row drawn below the table
issues.what: The page closes the earnings table with “Gross pay 4,098.08” under a rule. Our render draws it below the table as a loose line, with its amount beside the label.
issues.checks: Only a cells fault that matched the wrong copy (round 1, issue 7).
issues.claude: Added as major: the row leaves its table.
issues.often: Claude added 3 majors of this kind: a row out of its table, or into one.
issues.proposes: Keep it major.

issues.title: Letterspacing and small capitals lost
issues.what: The page sets “GUILD OF TIMBER ENGINEERS” with wide letterspacing, and the title in small capitals. Our render draws both at normal spacing, and the title in plain capitals.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Added as two minors, as the criteria say.
issues.often: Claude added 16 minors of these kinds.
issues.proposes: Keep them minor; add letterspacing to the IR later.

issues.title: A highlighted card's orange border drawn grey
issues.what: The page marks the Équipe card with an orange border. Our render draws it grey, like the other cards.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Claude added it as a minor, a frame in the wrong colour. But the orange marks the plan the page recommends, and the criteria call a colour that carries meaning major.
issues.often: Claude added 10 frame changes, 9 of them minor.
issues.proposes: Major, like the red order number: the colour carries meaning.

issues.title: A signature and a barcode not drawn
issues.what: The receipt prints a signature and a barcode. Our render draws two “signature” labels and the barcode's digits, but neither picture.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Added as minor: the criteria call figures minor.
issues.often: Claude added 13 figure faults, 12 of them minor.
issues.proposes: Keep it minor.

issues.title: Icons drawn as bullets
issues.what: The page starts each “Good to know” line with an icon: a clock, a mountain, a house. Our render draws plain bullets.
issues.checks: Nothing.
issues.claude: Added as minor: the criteria call figures minor.
issues.often: Claude added 5 of this kind.
issues.proposes: Keep it minor.

rounds.name: Round 5
rounds.title: Round 5: the build, before and after
rounds.intro: Round 4 is recorded: twelve agreed, and serif drawn as sans is now minor. The build is done: alignment, sizes, line breaks, faces, subscripts, copies, columns, and three new checks (text over text, beside, looks). This round shows real pages whose verdict moved, mostly pages you have not seen. The first three need your call: a card the checks now miss, an accent colour, a gap in a list. The rest confirm the new checks on new pages. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 5: the build's before and after on real pages, fourteen issues. Three ask for a call (a card moved that the checks now miss, a heading's accent colour, a gap in a list); eleven confirm the changed and new checks on pages mostly not seen before.

issues.title: A card's body drawn under the other two: the checks now miss it
issues.what: Three plan cards sit side by side. Our render keeps Starter and Fleet at the top, and draws Merlin Pro's price and features as an orange band below both.
issues.checks: Before: 6 majors, “their words alternate”. After: none. Each card stays in its own column, so the column rule (round 1) drops the interleaving, and no other check sees a card drawn below its neighbours.
issues.claude: A real major the build lost. Claude tried a check for it (a group printed beside another, drawn wholly below it): 1 true and 6 false on the 114 pages (columns of different lengths, cards staggered by a badge), so it was not kept.
issues.often: This page only, among the 114.
issues.proposes: Accept the miss: Claude's review names it as a major by eye, and the spec records it as a gap in the checks.

issues.title: A heading's accent colour drawn black
issues.what: “Des tarifs simples” is printed orange, in a script face; our render draws it dark. (The script drawn as a plain face is a separate fault, a major already.)
issues.checks: After: major, “colour lost”: the new looks check, a coloured text drawn neutral.
issues.claude: Here the colour is decoration, not meaning: the heading reads the same. The criteria make lost colour major where it marks something (red flags, an orange card frame), and a colour off in its family minor.
issues.often: 18 “colour lost” majors on 114 pages; about half are headings or titles like this one.
issues.proposes: Minor for a heading's or title's accent colour; major where coloured text or numbers carry meaning (as in the red notice, two issues on).

issues.title: A list torn by a gap, still in its column
issues.what: Key features sit beside the specifications on both. Our render draws the first feature, a blank gap, then the other five below the table's height.
issues.checks: Before: 4 majors, “features and specifications alternate”. After: none, and no check reports the gap.
issues.claude: The order is right: nothing is drawn among the specifications. The gap is spacing. Claude's own review had confirmed the 4 majors; that call was wrong.
issues.often: One page of this kind among the 114.
issues.proposes: No order fault; the gap is a minor (spacing), which Claude's review adds by eye.

issues.title: The recipe: one step drawn across the ingredients
issues.what: The method sits beside the ingredients on both. Step 3 (“Toast the hazelnuts…”) is drawn across the page, between the salad's ingredients and the dressing's.
issues.checks: Before: 8 majors, “ingredients and method alternate”. After: 1 major, step 3 “drawn across the column printed beside it”. The steps drawn as bullets stay major.
issues.claude: Right: columns kept side by side are no fault (round 1); the one step crossing into the ingredients is. One of the three known faults, now named exactly.
issues.often: Drawn across: 2 pages of 114 (this and c0522). Interleaving majors fell from 120 to 21.
issues.proposes: Keep: one major for the step drawn across.

issues.title: A section lost is not a section reordered
issues.what: Section 1 (“About you”: surname, first names, taxpayer reference…) is drawn as a black bar over an empty hatched box: its fields are missing from our render.
issues.checks: Before: 11 majors, “interleaved”, from three stray copies (“1”, “DD”, “MM”) paired with the signature table's. You rejected them. After: none; the missing words are reported as lost.
issues.claude: Right: a group with under half its words drawn is judged by the words check, not for order. Every interleaving you confirmed keeps 62% or more of its words.
issues.often: This page only: 11 rejected majors gone, no confirmed one lost.
issues.proposes: Keep.

issues.title: A red order number drawn black
issues.what: The order number, “encomenda n.º 2103-118”, is printed red and bold in the letter's first lines; our render draws it in the body's colour and weight.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “colour lost”.
issues.claude: Agree: the red marks the order the letter is about.
issues.often: 18 “colour lost” majors on 114 pages.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: A total drawn too faint to read
issues.what: The patient's total, “Estimated patient responsibility $2,965.78”, is printed white on a black bar; in our render it cannot be read on its ground.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “printed readable, drawn too faint to read”.
issues.claude: Agree: the total is unreadable.
issues.often: 11 majors on 11 pages.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: A headline drawn on dark boxes
issues.what: The headline is printed dark on the page's light ground; our render draws it white on dark boxes.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “printed on light, drawn on dark”.
issues.claude: Agree: the page reads differently.
issues.often: 17 majors.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: A pill drawn as a band across the page
issues.what: “Free entry · Family friendly” sits in a pill about a third of the page wide; our render fills the page's whole width.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “fill drawn another shape” (31% of the page → 100%).
issues.claude: Agree, per your round 2 call (a fill drawn the wrong shape is major).
issues.often: 9 majors.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: Fields drawn with no frame
issues.what: The applicant's fields are framed boxes on the page; our render draws them as plain rows with rules under them.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “frame missing” (9 fields).
issues.claude: Agree: the fields no longer read as boxes to fill in.
issues.often: 10 majors. A box drawn filled instead of framed (cards on a coloured ground) is now a minor: 12 minors, with chips and buttons.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: Buttons drawn as plain text are minor
issues.what: “Book a place” is an orange button under each workshop on the page; our render draws two of the three as plain text (the middle one keeps its button).
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: minor, “chip drawn plain”.
issues.claude: Per your round 2 call (buttons drawn as plain lines: minor).
issues.often: 9 minors.
issues.proposes: Keep minor.

issues.title: Paragraphs re-wrapped by their column are minor
issues.what: The letter's paragraphs wrap at different words than printed, in a slightly wider column.
issues.checks: Before: major, “broken differently”. After: minor, “re-wrapped” (8 breaks moved).
issues.claude: Per your round 3 call.
issues.often: Line-break majors fell from 92 to 25; 89 minors.
issues.proposes: Keep minor.

issues.title: A label and its value drawn over each other
issues.what: “Nom Delacroix”: label and value are apart on the page; our render draws them on top of each other.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “drawn over another word”.
issues.claude: Agree: unreadable. Your round 1 call.
issues.often: 13 majors.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: An amount torn from its label
issues.what: “Total to pay £28.74” is one row on the page; our render draws £28.74 on the next line, at the left.
issues.checks: Before: nothing. After: major, “printed beside, drawn under”.
issues.claude: Agree, per your round 1 call (labels torn from their amounts).
issues.often: 34 majors.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

rounds.name: Round 6
rounds.title: Round 6: two questions before the L3 run
rounds.intro: Round 5 is recorded: all fourteen agreed. L3 converts panel pages nobody has tuned on with today's pipeline, and ranks what goes wrong: the yardstick the GLM-OCR trial will be judged against. Two questions set its pages and its review. Click a decision: it saves and the next opens.
rounds.about: Round 6: spec 0022's two questions for the L3 baseline, neither asked in rounds 1-5: real PDF pages in the L3 set, and whether every page is opened. No render: questions for the plan.

issues.title: Add real PDF pages to the L3 set?
issues.what: The L3 set is 36 pages Claude wrote, four per family. None is a real PDF page; the panel holds nine. Below, three real PDF pages from dev, of the kinds Claude proposes to add: the panel's own stay unopened until the run.
issues.source_caption: Real PDF pages, from dev: a form, an invoice, a report
issues.checks: No real PDF page has been converted under today's limits: dev's one try, a dense form, ran out its 20 minutes.
issues.claude: The GLM-OCR trial is judged on this set, and its model learned from real pages. With none in the set, we cannot see whether it does better or worse on real pages than on pages Claude wrote. Five pages are a look, not a rate, so they are reported in their own line.
issues.often: About 40 minutes more at the usual pace, 100 at worst: 41 pages, about 5¾ hours (7½ at worst) instead of 5 (6).
issues.proposes: Add the panel's five PDF pages that are not dense: two application forms, an invoice, meeting minutes, an Italian status report (c0074, c0082, c0196, c0272, c0300). Picked by that rule, not by looking. The four dense ones (a tax form, two papers, a timetable) stay out: they would most likely run out their 20 minutes.

issues.title: Open and review every page of the L3 set?
issues.what: After the run the checks go over every page. The usual rule then opens only some (pages with a structural major, pages that moved, two per family), and the rest are judged by the checks alone.
issues.checks: The checks still miss some faults (a card drawn below its neighbours, a list torn by a gap) and still raise false ones: over L2's 114 reviewed pages, 23 majors and 32 minors Claude had rejected.
issues.claude: This set is the yardstick the GLM-OCR trial is judged against, so every page should carry a call made by eye. Opened pages count as seen: no fix is ever pinned on them, and the vault stays the sealed exam.
issues.often: Claude's time only; no model run.
issues.proposes: Yes: Claude opens every page and reviews it by the criteria. You check, as in L2, every page where Claude's call overturns a check, plus two at random.

rounds.name: Round 7
rounds.title: Round 7: the L3 review, fifteen spot checks
rounds.intro: Round 6 is recorded: the L3 set took the panel's five PDF pages that are not dense (41 pages), and every page was opened. Claude has now reviewed all 37 converted pages; four timed out. Issues 1 to 9 are every check fault Claude rejected, on 10 pages. Issues 10 to 13 are new kinds of fault Claude added, which no check raises. Issues 14 and 15 are two of Claude's confirmed majors, drawn at random. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 7: spec 0022's spot checks of Claude's review of L3-baseline (37 pages opened). 1-9 cover every rejected check fault (27 faults on 10 pages); 10-13 are one example of each kind of added major not shown before; 14-15 are confirmed check majors drawn at random (seed 7) on pages not otherwise in this round.

issues.title: A ligature read as a spelling mistake
issues.what: This PDF page prints “specific” and “fitness” with an fi ligature (fi joined into one glyph). Our render draws both words as printed.
issues.checks: Major, three times: “specifc → specific”, “ftness → fitness”.
issues.claude: A false alarm. The PDF's text layer drops the ligature, and this check compares that raw text without the page's spelling map. The words check already uses the map.
issues.often: 3 majors on 1 page; PDF pages only.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: map each source word through the page's spelling map before comparing. Pinned by a unit test with its own map, no panel page.

issues.title: Repeated words paired with the wrong card
issues.what: Six dish cards each print “Serves 2” and a price. Our render draws the cards one under another (a real fault, counted on its own), but each card's words stay together, 01 to 06 in order.
issues.checks: Major, four times: two cards' words “alternate in the output's reading order”, card 1 against card 6 among them.
issues.claude: A false alarm. The check pairs the six copies of “Serves 2” by where their neighbours moved. On a page whose grid became one column, that sends card 6's copy to card 1's.
issues.often: 4 majors on 1 page.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: re-pair copies of a word only where their neighbours moved together; otherwise keep the pairing in reading order.

decided.note: this is more a layout fault then alignment since is completely different from the 2x3 cards layout and all sequential along page

issues.title: A line beside a heading counted inside its section
issues.what: “Tuesday to Saturday 5:00 to 9:00 pm” is printed top right, beside the heading “Small plates”. Our render draws it there too.
issues.checks: Major, five times: “Small plates” and each card “alternate in the output's reading order”.
issues.claude: A false alarm. The check takes everything right of the heading into its section, the hours included. The HTML writes the hours after the table, but the eye reads them where they are drawn.
issues.often: 5 majors on 1 page.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: a heading's section leaves out what is printed beside the heading.

issues.title: A table in the right column called “under another heading”
issues.what: Section 1's price table sits in the right column under “Section 1 — Fasteners”, on the page and in our render. “Your account rep” heads the left sidebar.
issues.checks: Major: “printed under ‘Section 1 — Fasteners’, drawn under ‘Your account rep’”.
issues.claude: A false alarm. The check reads the HTML top to bottom; the eye reads each column. Same on c0334, where “Residents are asked…” is called under “Charges”.
issues.often: 2 majors on 2 pages.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: judge which heading a block is under column by column, as the order check already does.

decided.note: first card of the set of three has replicated wrong format title - this is the main issue as it replicates it not even sure what was flagged error but yes is major

issues.title: A drop cap called a merged word
issues.what: The notice opens with a large drop cap “N” followed by “otice”: the reader reads “Notice”. Our render draws “Notice” as one word in body type.
issues.checks: Major: “n otice → notice”, two words merged into one.
issues.claude: A false alarm on the word: “Notice” is what the page says. The lost drop cap is real, and is added as a minor.
issues.often: 1 major on 1 page.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: a drop cap joined to the rest of its word is that word, not a merge.

issues.title: Words on a dark tab, called “drawn on dark”
issues.what: On this PDF page, “Part II” is white on a black tab, and “Signature” beside it is on white. Our render draws the same.
issues.checks: Major: “printed on light, drawn on dark”.
issues.claude: A false alarm: the check takes one ground for the whole line, but this line sits on two. A similar case on c0082: a green band drawn green, where only its heading's colour changed (a minor).
issues.often: 2 majors on 2 pages.
issues.proposes: No fix yet: both cases are lines that sit on two grounds. Fix it if more cases turn up.

issues.title: A table with every rule drawn, called merged
issues.what: The passenger table has two rules between its columns and one between its rows. Our render draws all three.
issues.checks: Major: “1 of the 7 rules the page draws between cells are not drawn”.
issues.claude: A false alarm by eye: every rule between two cells is drawn. Claude cannot find the rule the check counts as missing.
issues.often: 1 major on 1 page.
issues.proposes: Look into the check's rule count on this table before changing anything.

issues.title: A line where the page puts it, called moved
issues.what: “Spring offer ends 30 June 2024” sits at the right end of the green bar, on the page and in our render.
issues.checks: Minor: “printed right, drawn left”.
issues.claude: A false alarm: the line is where the page puts it. The same on c0070: the date sits flush left under its label “DATE” in both; the whole field moved right, which is spacing.
issues.often: 2 minors on 2 pages.
issues.proposes: No alignment fault. Your round 3 line holds: raise alignment only when the line itself moves.

decided.note: agree this is just text bold and color with justification so minor is ok but an alignment issue per se just result of wrong text show-specs

issues.title: A heading judged though it is not drawn at all
issues.what: This PDF page's whole PG7.2026 table, heading included, is not drawn: the straightening step crops it away, and those lost words are confirmed. Our render opens with PG8.2026 (marked). The checks still judge PG7's heading for structure, size and weight, from a few of its words matched to other lines.
issues.checks: Five faults on PG7's heading: “table not kept”, “heading not kept”, two “sizes out of proportion”, “bold lost”.
issues.claude: Rejected: there is nothing drawn to judge, and the loss is already counted word by word. Similar on c0382: “Try it” is called bold lost, but it is drawn bold; its fault, the line split in two, is counted already.
issues.often: 6 faults on 2 pages.
issues.proposes: Fix the check: skip the structure and type checks for a block mostly not drawn, as the order check already does.

issues.title: A card drawn in a sliver: its words cannot be read
issues.what: The fourth step, “4 Roll out everywhere / Zara Burrows updates the till, the website and the shelf labels in one weekend.”, cannot be seen in our render. Its Zone is drawn as a white column a pixel or two wide (marked), and its dark words fall one per line down the dark ground beside it.
issues.checks: Nothing for these words: they are all in the HTML. The checks see the page's height (1.75) and some words drawn twice.
issues.claude: Major: the step cannot be read. A small figure Zone over its “4” takes the card's place in the row.
issues.often: 2 pages: this one, and c0596, where “at” is drawn at 0.30 of the body and “Meet at:” reads “Meet.:”.
issues.proposes: Major. A new check: a line drawn narrower than its longest word, or smaller than a third of the body, is unreadable.

issues.title: An accent word drawn as a link
issues.what: The slide's headline prints “beacon” in orange. Our render draws it blue and underlined, like a link.
issues.checks: Nothing: the checks compare colours only within a colour family, and none looks for an underline.
issues.claude: Major: it changes what the word seems to be (a link the page does not have). Round 5 made a heading's accent drawn black a minor; this is a different case, because a new meaning is added.
issues.often: 2 pages: here (major), and an email address drawn as a link on c0555 (minor).
issues.proposes: Major when an accent word is drawn as a link; minor for an address the page prints plain.

issues.title: A bar chart drawn as loose numbers
issues.what: The page draws a bar chart of costs by quarter. Our render has no chart: its axis becomes table rows ($120 … $0), and the bar values a column of loose numbers.
issues.checks: They see words moved, the height and the legend's order. None says the chart is gone.
issues.claude: Major: no value can be tied to its quarter or its farm any more. The chart's Zone is classed as a table.
issues.often: 1 page.
issues.proposes: Major. A chart is drawn as a figure (its pixels) unless its data can be read whole.

issues.title: Each card drawn as two boxes: the icon apart from its text
issues.what: Each of the four pale cards holds an icon and two lines. Our render draws the icon in a small box of its own, and the text in a second box beside it.
issues.checks: Nothing about the cards: the fill check compares the ground under each line, and the text is on pale green in both.
issues.claude: Major, a fill drawn another shape: it no longer reads as one card. The card fills are found, then given to no Zone.
issues.often: Added on 11 pages: cards, bands and headers split into one box per Zone.
issues.proposes: Major. The fill check should also compare each fill's outline with what is drawn.

issues.title: A BMI range drawn under “Measure”
issues.what: The table's last row prints “BMI” under Measure and “18.5 to 24.9 kg/m2” under Range. Our table ends at “Peak flow”, and “BMI” and its range come back as two loose lines under it.
issues.checks: Major: “drawn under ‘Measure’, printed under ‘Range’”.
issues.claude: Agree, major: the table answer stopped one row short, and that row's two cells were read again as loose lines.
issues.often: Cells in the wrong column: 5 pages.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: A line drawn twice: as a title and as its own first line
issues.what: “A calculator may be used.” is printed once. Our render draws it twice: as the section's title, then again as its first line.
issues.checks: Major: its words are “drawn 1 more time than printed”.
issues.claude: Agree, major: the caption pass took the line as the Zone's title, and the body kept it too.
issues.often: Words invented: 24 pages; a title repeated in its body: 4 pages.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

rounds.name: Round 8
rounds.title: Round 8: four questions before the GLM-OCR trial
rounds.intro: Round 7 is recorded: all fifteen agreed. P1 builds the GLM-OCR trial: GLM-OCR cuts the page into blocks and reads them, a new adapter turns its blocks into our pages, and our looks and renderer draw them. Four questions set where it is built, on which pages, how long its run may take, and one GLM-OCR setting. Click a decision: it saves and the next opens.
rounds.about: Round 8: spec 0023's four questions for P1, none asked in rounds 1-7: the branch's base, the build pages, the time for the 41-page run, and whether to read the regions GLM-OCR discards by default. No render: questions for the plan; Q2 shows three of the eleven dev pages, Q4 the payslip with the discarded lines marked.

issues.title: Build the GLM-OCR trial on a branch from level-up?
issues.what: The plan says to branch from develop. But the corpus, the checks, the batch runner and L3's frozen run were all made on level-up, after develop was cut. From develop, the trial would have none of them.
issues.checks: level-up holds everything L1 to L3 built. develop stops at the S14 baseline of 2026-10-23.
issues.claude: The trial needs the corpus to pick its pages, the batch runner to convert them, and the checks and L3's run to compare against. From develop, all of them would have to be copied across.
issues.often: Nothing. level-up itself takes nothing of the trial until P2 decides.
issues.proposes: Branch poc-parser-first from level-up's head.

issues.title: Build the adapter on eleven dev pages, then run the L3 set?
issues.what: The adapter, the new code that turns GLM-OCR's blocks into our pages, is built and judged by eye on dev pages only. Below, three of the eleven Claude proposes: a flyer, the ticket and a real PDF purchase order.
issues.source_caption: Three of the eleven build pages, all from dev
issues.checks: No page has been drawn by GLM-OCR and our renderer yet. The plan names the kinds of page where it may go wrong.
issues.claude: Picked by a rule, not by looking: every dev page the plan names for a risk (the designed pages: flyer, quiz, ticket, pricing, catalogue; side-by-side panels: payslip, recipe, datasheet; the hardest table: the lab report), plus dev's two real PDF pages of the kinds in the L3 set (an application form, a purchase order). No panel page is opened before the run.
issues.often: GLM-OCR reads each page once, about 20 seconds; after that each change to the adapter is drawn again in seconds, with no model.
issues.proposes: Build on these eleven dev pages; then convert the 41 L3 pages once, with the adapter frozen.

issues.title: Run the 41 pages without waiting, if they fit in two hours?
issues.what: GLM-OCR read each of five dev pages in 8 to 36 seconds today, its layout model and its reader together. Today's pipeline took 6.6 hours for the 41 L3 pages.
issues.checks: GLM-OCR alone: 8 to 36 s a page. Our looks and render add to it; the eleven build pages measure the whole page's time before the run.
issues.claude: At a minute a page the 41 take about 40 minutes. The same 20-minute page limit as L3 keeps the two runs' timeouts comparable.
issues.often: Under an hour expected, against L3's 6.6 hours. Local model time only; the review afterwards is Claude's.
issues.proposes: Keep the 20-minute page limit. Before the run Claude gives you the time measured on the build pages, and starts if it is under two hours; over two hours, it stops and waits for your go.

issues.title: Read the headers and footers GLM-OCR throws away?
issues.what: By default GLM-OCR discards six kinds of block: page headers, footers, footnotes, page numbers, side notes and references. On the payslip below, the five lines boxed in red would be read by nobody: the company, PAYSLIP, the address, the pay period and the footer.
issues.source_caption: The payslip: in red, the lines GLM-OCR discards by default
issues.checks: Our pipeline reads every line it finds, and L3 counts each line lost as a major.
issues.claude: These are lost by a setting, not by a misreading: on most pages that is a major fault by design, and the comparison would measure the setting rather than GLM-OCR. Reading them is one line of its configuration; its boxes, labels, order and weights stay its own.
issues.often: Most pages print a header or a footer: on the payslip, 5 of its 13 blocks.
issues.proposes: Read all six kinds as text, each header and footer drawn as a header or a footer.

rounds.name: Round 9
rounds.title: Round 9: the D2 review, eleven spot checks, then P2
rounds.intro: Round 8 is recorded: all four agreed. D2 converted all 41 L3 pages in 18 minutes; Claude reviewed every page. Issues 1 to 4 are every check fault Claude rejected. Issues 5 to 9 are new kinds of fault Claude added. Issues 10 and 11 are two of Claude's confirmed majors, drawn at random. Issue 12 is P2's question. Click a decision: it saves and the next issue opens.
rounds.about: Round 9: spec 0023's spot checks of Claude's review of P1-D2-L3 (41 pages opened). 1-4 cover every rejected check fault (8 faults on 6 pages); 5-9 are one example of each kind of added major not shown before; 10-11 are confirmed check majors drawn at random (seed 9) on pages not otherwise in this round; 12 is P2's decision.

issues.title: Ticks drawn as √, called lost
issues.what: The status report prints ✓ for done (1), ☐ for open (2) and ✗ for blocked (3). GLM-OCR writes them as √, □ and ×, and our render draws what it writes (marked). The meaning is unchanged: every √ is a printed ✓.
issues.checks: Major, three times: ✓ printed 13 times and not drawn, ✗ twice; and □ drawn 6 times, not printed. Also on c0316 (✓ three times) and c0342 (✓ three times).
issues.claude: A false alarm, as major. By your rule of 2026-11-01 a look-alike mark is a minor: Claude rejected the four majors and added one minor “mark changed” on each page. The ☐ that GLM-OCR dropped outright (5 of 11 here) stay major.
issues.often: 4 majors rejected on 3 pages; D2 only (today's reader writes ✓).
issues.proposes: Fix the check: √ ✓ ✔, × ✗ ✕ and □ ☐ are look-alikes, a minor “mark changed”, never lost plus invented. Pinned on a dev page.

issues.title: A drawn tick box written as □, called invented
issues.what: Line 1 of this PDF form prints an empty tick box (1). GLM-OCR writes it as the character □, and our render draws it in place. Line 2's box (2) is not written at all, and our render has no box there.
issues.checks: Major: □ drawn once and not printed. Nothing for line 2's box: the PDF's text layer has no character for either box.
issues.claude: Rejected: the □ is the page's own box, drawn where the page draws it. Claude added line 2's lost box as a major “mark lost”: an empty box lost changes what the form asks.
issues.often: 1 page; the PDF pages draw their boxes as lines, not characters.
issues.proposes: Rejected as invented; line 2's lost box major. No check change: the PDF gives the check no box to compare.

issues.title: A heading on a green band, called “printed on light”
issues.what: This PDF prints the section heading in white on a green band. Our render draws the band green and the heading white on it (smaller, a separate fault).
issues.checks: Major: “printed on light, drawn on green”.
issues.claude: A false alarm: the page prints it on green. This page's HTML draws the band as a separate box under the heading, not as its parent, and the check reads the ground from the heading's parents: the white body.
issues.often: 1 page. Round 7's c0074 tab was the same kind: the ground read where the page does not paint it.
issues.proposes: Rejected. The check could read a line's ground from what is painted under it, not from its parents; one page, so recorded for now.

issues.title: Two blocks side by side, called interleaved
issues.what: The patient details (left) and the observations table (right) sit side by side, and our render draws them side by side, in their places.
issues.checks: Minor: their words alternate in the output's HTML, “drawn side by side as printed”.
issues.claude: A false alarm: drawn as the page prints them; the order of words in the HTML is not seen.
issues.often: 1 minor on 1 page.
issues.proposes: Rejected. The check could skip blocks it finds drawn side by side as printed.

issues.title: Two fields read as one: labels on one line, values on the next
issues.what: The invitation prints PLACE over “The Long Room, Wrexham” and, beside it, DRESS over “Smart casual”. Our render draws “PLACE DRESS”, then “The Long Room, Wrexham Smart casual”: whose value is whose is lost.
issues.checks: Nothing: every word is there, in order line by line.
issues.claude: Major: a reader cannot tell the dress code from the place. GLM-OCR takes the two fields for one block and writes it line by line across both.
issues.often: 3 pages (c0121's four field pairs, c0515, c0342's labels over values); the parser's reading.
issues.proposes: Major, a new kind: “label parted from its value”.

issues.title: A formula drawn as its LaTeX source
issues.what: The textbook prints t½ = ln 2 / k as a set formula. Our render draws “$$”, “t _ {1 / 2} = \ln 2 / k”, “$$”: GLM-OCR writes display formulas as LaTeX, and the adapter draws the source.
issues.checks: Words lost and invented (kt, approx, left, right…), and “hint” split letter by letter.
issues.claude: Major: the formula cannot be read as printed. Our side: the adapter turns inline maths into characters but not display formulas.
issues.often: 1 page, three formulas; any page with display maths.
issues.proposes: Major, a new kind: “formula drawn as source”, made at the adapter.

issues.title: Markup drawn as text: “4^{1}$”
issues.what: The recipe prints SERVES 4¹. Our render draws “4^{1}$”: GLM-OCR writes the raised 1 as broken LaTeX, and it is drawn as written. On c0234 the reader's bold markers are drawn too: “**Action:**”.
issues.checks: Minor: “a part printed raised, drawn inline after a mark”.
issues.claude: Major: braces, a caret and a dollar sign are drawn that the page does not print, an invented mark.
issues.proposes: Major: “mark invented”.

issues.title: A full-width table drawn in half the page
issues.what: The ticket prints its passenger table across the whole ticket (1). Our render draws it in the left half, its cells wrapping (“Bags:1 / hold,1 / hand”), and the passenger icon from inside the table alone in a white box in the right half (2).
issues.checks: Rules merged, bold lost, the page 1.51 times as tall: not the half width.
issues.claude: Major: the table is drawn as a narrow column beside an empty box. GLM-OCR gives the icon inside the table a region of its own; the adapter bands it beside the table.
issues.often: 2 pages (c0523; c0388's icons beside their list, drawn one word a line).
issues.proposes: Major: “drawn in a lane”, made at the adapter.

issues.title: A black paragraph drawn red
issues.what: The magazine prints the paragraph “Arjun Patel, who has kept bees…” in black; the pull quote under it is red. Our render draws the paragraph red.
issues.checks: Nothing: the colour checks look for colour lost, not added.
issues.claude: Major: red marks the quote; a red paragraph reads as part of it. The paragraph's measured colour came from the quote's lines.
issues.often: 1 page.
issues.proposes: Major, a new kind: “colour added”.

issues.title: A PDF form read only to its first header rows
issues.what: GLM-OCR takes the whole voucher for one table and writes only its header rows (render, right). The title, the payment and certification sections and the numbered notes (marked) are not read: 143 words.
issues.checks: Major, among them: “signature” printed twice and not drawn.
issues.claude: Agree, major: made by the parser's reading. Today's pipeline timed out on this page.
issues.often: Words lost on 19 pages; three pages lose most of a section this way (c0097, c0196, c0300).
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: Bold header cells drawn regular
issues.what: This PDF table prints its header row and its total row bold. Our render draws “Descrizione obiettivo”, “FTE” and the total's 9 regular.
issues.checks: Major: “bold printed, regular drawn” (7 blocks).
issues.claude: Agree, major: those cells measured regular.
issues.often: Bold lost: 35 pages.
issues.proposes: Keep major.

issues.title: P2: take D2 as the converter?
issues.what: D2: GLM-OCR cuts the page and reads it, our adapter maps its blocks, our looks and renderer draw them. On the 41 L3 pages, against today's pipeline (L3-baseline), both reviewed page by page.
issues.checks: Time: 26 s a page against 577 s (18 minutes against 6.6 hours), no timeouts against 4. On the 37 pages both converted: 660 majors against 651; 13 pages better, 7 worse, 17 the same. D2 also converted the 4 pages today's lost. Words invented: 7 pages against 24; numbered steps drawn as bullets: none against 10.
issues.claude: Net gain, and fast enough to measure every change on the whole panel. The worse pages are named: c0097 and c0441 (the parser misses a sidebar, a name), c0064 and c0129 (accents and names misread), c0115 (four lines in no region), c0070 (broken table HTML), c0387 (stacked columns).
issues.often: Parser side: a box read as one table and only its grid read (c0097, c0196, c0300); misread names and accents. Our side, fixable: tables with spans left unmeasured by locate (12 pages), $ amounts taken for maths, stacked columns drawn under, formulas drawn as source.
issues.proposes: Take D2. Next, L5 on D2: our side's faults first, each reproduced on a dev page, the parser's weights untouched. Disagree to keep today's; a mix (which side from which arm) in the note.
